purpose: Single contract for intentional platform default differences across Rust serde defaults, Kotlin MhrvConfig, and importer fallbacks.

rust_desktop_cli.socks5_note: Serde default is omitted/null: SOCKS5 listener disabled until socks5_port is set. README and config*.example.json conventionally use 8086 beside HTTP 8085.
rust_desktop_cli.parallel_relay_note: Serde default is u8 zero: off for explicit parallel relay firing unless runtime tuning or imports raise it. Effective relay concurrency may still use round-robin when unset.
rust_desktop_cli.coalesce_note: Zero lets the Rust runtime derive full-mode adaptive coalescing timings. Kotlin defaults to concrete 10/1000 ms to match the current low-latency full-tunnel coalescing profile.

android.rationale_ports_vs_desktop: Android keeps loopback proxies on 8080/1081 so built-in HELP copy and Proxy-only guides match historically shipped presets; Rust desktop/CLI uses 8085/8086 to reduce collisions with common local services.
android.rationale_google_ip_vs_rust: Android presets a historically tested Google-anycast edge for captive/mobile paths; Rust desktop favors 216.239.38.120 with scan guidance. Imported configs overwrite both surfaces.
android.rationale_parallel_relay_vs_rust: Android defaults `parallel_relay` to `1` (single parallel fan-out knob in the simplified UI stack). Rust defaults to `0` (off unless user or auto-tuning enables higher fan-out); desktop examples often raise it.
android.rationale_coalesce_ms_vs_rust: Rust treats `coalesce_*_ms` as `0` when omitted (derive runtime-internal defaults). Android seeds `10`/`1000` so mobile saves match the current compiled low-latency profile unless the user explicitly restores older, slower coalescing.
